summary: Kootenai NF lookout in Lincoln County: a pole L-4 tower listed for 1934 and now gone; sources give no removal date and do not describe the summit today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no removal date or cause given in any source read

events.note: Record lists a pole L-4 tower for 1934

evidence.supports: landmark list places the mountain in the Yaak River Valley
landmark entry: tepees set up at what is now Tepee Springs, at the mountain's base; the entry does not explain the name
evidence.quote: In the early days, the Indians erected their tepees at what is now Tepee Springs, located at the base of the mountain.

notes_for_editor: Only one lookout-specific source: a short firelookout.com entry with no staffing or fire history. The landmark-names list places the mountain in the Yaak River Valley and describes tepees at its base, but it does not say how the mountain got its name, so the story does not claim it does. It does not support the tower itself. The Archives West Lolo National Forest finding aid (ark:80444/xv96920) lists an item titled Teepee Mountain, 1931, but it sits in a Lolo collection and was not confirmed to be this Lincoln County peak, so it is left out. Access is left unset. Possible next steps: Kootenai NF history or Montana newspapers. Story is about 130 words.
